answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-personhood: each agent must bind to a unique, non-transferable human credential before it can earn or attest, mapping identities 1:1 to real people. Running 1,000 sybils then needs 1,000 distinct verified humans, not 1,000 cheap keypairs, so cost scales with the scarce resource. The attacker's only break is forging or renting uniqueness proofs, yet each reused human trips a duplicate-detection beacon that revokes the clones. Verified slots stay sparse as outposts on bare tundra and onboarding is juniper-slow by design, so no farm can mass-mint personhood.
